body.x: Docenty.AI (CEO Ilgu Lee) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. At the K-Startup Pavilion, it will present its industry-specific AI chatbot solutions.

Specializing in AI solutions for automating business processes, Docenty has focused on tailoring its offerings to diverse industries such as construction, e-commerce, finance, and law. With partnerships spanning SMEs, large corporations, and government agencies, the company has amassed extensive data to provide efficient and customizable automation solutions.

At CES, Docenty will unveil its advanced large language model (LLM)- based platform for building customized chatbots. This solution supports basic chatbot functions and integrates features to enhance customer experiences in e-commerce, setting it apart from competitors in terms of functionality and convenience.

The platform excels in understanding conversational context and intent, delivering precise answers while offering personalized product recommendations. Its fully automated system enables seamless 24/7 customer support, improving service quality and operational efficiency.

Docenty’s recommendation algorithm analyzes purchase history, preferences, and user behavior, leveraging comprehensive datasets to provide reliable and tailored suggestions. The more data it accumulates—from customer interactions to product reviews—the better it refines its predictive capabilities.
Additionally, the platform's analytics capabilities allow businesses to optimize inventory management by forecasting demand based on aggregated customer insights.

"Unlike many competitors that charge exorbitant fees for personalized systems or offer subpar solutions at lower costs, Docenty strikes a balance by delivering high-quality, industry-specific chatbots at reasonable prices," a company representative explained. "Our technology helps clients automate tasks and maximize marketing effectiveness."

Docenty aims to expand its domestic client base while using CES as a launchpad to build global brand recognition. By showcasing its cutting-edge technology, the company seeks to strengthen its position as a leader in AI and NLP innovation and forge new partnerships in international markets.

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
